title: Introduce dynamic baseline slicing and noise-aware CI gate for p95 tokens/sec regressions
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Problem: PRs occasionally introduce subtle performance regressions that only show up for specific slices (long sequences, 8-bit quantized models, or particular GPU families). Current CI gates use coarse baselines and rigid thresholds, causing both false positives on noisy runs and missed regressions in underrepresented slices.

Proposal: Implement a dynamic baseline slicing system and a noise-aware CI gate that: 1) builds and stores multi-dimensional baselines keyed by model, sequence length bucket, hardware family, and cache-warmth (cold/warm); 2) applies statistical tests with bootstraped confidence intervals and minimum-sample heuristics; 3) refuses PR merges when the p95 tokens/sec or p95 latency shows a statistically significant regression beyond configurable delta; and 4) surfaces automated triage hints pointing to candidate changes (kernel, batching, kv-cache). This ticket implements the CI-side gating and the baseline selection logic; baseline population/maintenance is an adjacent task but is included in rollout steps.
acceptance_criteria: CI can compute a relevant baseline slice for any PR execution given metadata (model, seq_len_bucket, hardware, cache_state)
Gate computes p95 tokens/sec and corresponding 95% bootstrap confidence interval from CI-run samples
Gate fails PRs only when the observed p95 is worse than the baseline lower bound by >5% and p-value < 0.01 (configurable)
Gate records detailed failure reason to PR comment with links to example traces, config used, and suggested triage steps
Baseline selection supports fallback to coarser slices with documented priority order and logs fallback events
implementation_plan: Add metadata tags to CI load harness runs (model, seq_length_bucket, device_family, warm_cache_flag)
Extend baseline store schema to support multi-dimensional keys and rolling windows (time-series index)
Implement baseline selector that picks exact match or falls back in this order: exact slice -> aggregated seq bucket -> model-family aggregate -> global baseline
Integrate non-parametric bootstrap sampling (1000 resamples by default) to compute CI for p95 tokens/sec and p95 latency
Add gating evaluation step in PR pipeline that compares observed metric to baseline and posts annotated results
Create lightweight dashboard for baseline health and slice coverage (counts, staleness)
test_plan: Unit tests for baseline selector logic, deterministic tests using stored trace replays, and end-to-end CI runs against canary PRs. E2E tests include synthetic regressions introduced via a toy kernel change to validate detection sensitivity and false-positive rate. We'll also run a 2-week shadow mode where gate computes verdicts but does not block merges, collecting statistics on false-positives/negatives.

decisions: Use non-parametric bootstrap CI for p95 estimation instead of assuming normality
Adopt multi-dimensional baselines keyed by (model, seq_len_bucket, device_family, cache_state)
Set initial gating delta to 5% with p-value threshold 0.01 and minimum-sample 30
Shadow mode rollout for two weeks before enabling blocking merges
tradeoffs: Tight slice granularity reduces missed regressions but increases baseline staleness and storage. We choose a pragmatic middle ground with seq_len buckets and device-family aggregates plus a staleness policy (auto-aggregate slices older than 14 days). Computational cost of bootstrap in CI increases runtime; mitigated by caching baseline CI and doing full bootstrap only on suspicious deltas.
monitoring_and_alerting: Gate outcomes emitted to metrics (gates.evaluated, gates.failed, gates.fallbacks, gate_latency_ms). Alert if fallback rate > 10% for 24h or false-positive rate in shadow mode > 5% over two weeks. Failure comments surface links to flamegraphs and p95 distributions.
rollback_plan: If gate causes excessive false positives after rollout, revert to shadow mode and revert the gating step in the PR pipeline. Baseline store changes are backwards compatible; revert gating only requires a single pipeline toggle.
post_mortem_trigger: Trigger post-mortem if a gating change blocks >10 customer-impacting merges in a rolling 48h window or if we miss a regression that later causes >5% customer impact.
notes: Consider experimenting with EWMAC (exponentially weighted moving average control) for very high-frequency slices later
